influence the direction and work with team members who are hands-on with these
activities.
-We meet with clients about once per week through the duration of their project and maintenance. Many of those meetings happen over Zoom. During those meetings, you’ll present the status of work by the team, gain feedback and then create work tickets to incorporate the meeting’s discussion into actionable items that designers and developers can work on.

You’ll be sending and receiving emails from clients that are giving you new information
and feedback about their project. Expert management of email communications is key.
- In between these meetings, you’ll be monitoring the progress of the tasks that you’ve
created and managing project budgets. This includes making sure that tickets are done
in time for your next scheduled client update as well as adjusting work objectives, client
expectations and meetings as necessary.

ideas to designers to implement visually. While you might not be a graphic designer,
you’ll leverage your “good eye” for design regularly. You’ll organize and create PowerPoints / instruction for design and development feedback from clients.

client has submitted the content we need to build a website and making sure that it
looks right on the page. In addition, you’ll be making sure that the objectives of the
website are met. While you might not be a coder, you’ll feel comfortable using most aspects of Shopify and WordPress, and be capable of communicating with those on our team that
build websites to make sure the website comes together correctly.

embodied in the design and final build of the website.
● Having a sense of accomplishment as you see projects come together and as you find
solutions to challenging problems.

Your background and experience probably includes...

● Working in a position that places high value on customer service.
● Working with media and marketing or advertising (and hopefully, websites!)

● Having fun!
● Familiarity with HTML, CSS and other web technologies is a plus,
● Working in a leadership capacity, including keen decision making abilities especially
when you might not have all the information at hand,

● Working in an B2B environment and thinking like a business owner,
● Managing projects according to a budget.
● Working as a member of a team as well as independently,
● Working with deadlines and budgets,

-Some Wordpress / Shopify background would be great, but trainable

title: GIS Map with Code
description:
We need a script to compute the distance between points along a network. Both spatial data sets come from HIFLD. The points are natural gas compressor stations ([link removed] The network is a map of US natural gas pipelines ([link removed] 

Consider the example (attached: Compressor_distance.png): Points A and B represent two compressor stations on the pipeline network (green multiline strings). In order to calculate the distance between A and B, we don't want the shortest distance (represented by the red line segment). The correct way to calculate the distance is highlighted in yellow, which is the distance between points A and B measured along the pipeline network. 

To this end, we are looking to hire someone to write code that processes these shapefiles and performs the following tasks. 

1. Create a continuous pipeline map. The HIFLD pipeline map contains many separate line segments. We want to snap all segments within some tolerance (say 500m - subject to change) together, to create a continuous network. 
2. Snap compressor stations to the pipeline network. Points in the compressor station shapefile may not actually touch the pipeline network. We want to snap each compressor station to the closest point on the pipeline network (within say 500 feet). 
3. Calculate the distance between the compressor stations along the pipeline network. For each individual compressor station(point), identify the closest 10 compressor stations along the pipeline network. The final product should be a list of compressor station pairs and the distance between them along the network. 

Please note that we require a well-organized script utilizing either Python and QGIS or R and the simple features (sf) package. Simply producing a map and the distances without a script that can be edited is not sufficient.

title: Website designer needed
description:
1 page website design needed
What Is a Web Designer?

A web designer is responsible for designing the layout, visual elements, and usability of a website. Their goal is to create something that is not only visually appealing but also streamlined and easy to use. There are many types of web designers, including information architects (who establish a site’s structure and hierarchy for SEO), visual designers (who make sure a site is aesthetically pleasing), and user experience designers (who ensure that the site’s design supports the user’s experience).

Example of a Web Designer Job Description

In this section, we will cover a sample job description, exploring the daily responsibilities and necessary qualifications of a web designer. 

The Job Overview

We are looking for a web designer to join our team. You will be involved in the development of our website, from the earliest conception to final release. As our web designer, you will work with the front-end developer to create intuitive, attractive user interfaces to engage customers. Your duties will include taking requirements, creating mock-ups, and designing layouts while balancing the usability, visual appeal, and technical feasibility of the designs. You will also have the opportunity to plan and execute projects, as well as improve the overall quality of the website.

Responsibilities

Below are some of the responsibilities a web designer is expected to assume:  

Create wireframes or mockups for web pages and applications
Design layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop devices
Create branding and identity systems for websites, apps, and other media
Design graphics, icons, and logos
Design custom WordPress themes
Work with developers to implement visual elements of websites
Research and evaluate new design trends
Establish and maintain design standards and best practices
Job Qualifications and Skill Sets

Below are the qualifications expected of a web designer:

Proficiency with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Bachelor’s degree in design or a related field
Experience as a graphic designer or in a related field
Demonstrable graphic design skills with a strong portfolio
Proficiency with required desktop publishing tools, including Photoshop, InDesign, QuarkXPress, and Illustrator
A strong eye for visual design and composition
Effective time management skills and the ability to meet deadlines
Understanding of marketing, production, website design, corporate identity, product packaging, advertisements, and multimedia design
Experience with computer-aided design

Here's an example of what we want the app to be:

Create a Group: The app would allow you to create a group of people, such as your friends or family members, who are sharing expenses.

Add Bills: You can add bills to the app, either by manually entering the details of each bill or by scanning a receipt using your phone's camera.

Split the Bill: Once you have added all the bills, the app would allow you to split the total cost in different ways such as equal split, by percentage, or by specific items.

Choose Payment Method: The app would allow you to choose the payment method for each person. For example, one person may pay for everything and others pay their share through the app.

Track Payments: The app would keep track of who has paid their share and who still owes money. It would also send reminders to those who have not paid their share.

Finalize the Split: Once everyone has paid their share, the app would allow you to finalize the split and send a detailed report to each person with the amount they owe or are owed.

Some additional features that may be included in a bill splitting app are the ability to split expenses between different groups, integration with popular payment apps, and the ability to split bills in different currencies.

title: Minecraft Lifesteal Plugin
description:
I'm looking for someone to make me a custom life steal plugin for my Minecraft server. I run a server of about 150 people and I'm looking to get a new life steal plugin because I would like features that I don't see anywhere else. If you don't know what life steal is, here's a short description.

Life steal allows players to kill other players to take their hearts. Each player will start on the server with their default health value of 10 hearts and a heart should be removed when dying to natural causes. Likewise, a heart would be removed when dying to a player, but in this case, the heart that is lost when dying to the player, is given to the player that eliminated them. When the player dies to a natural cause such as fall damage, a mob, lava, drowning, etc. they just lose a heart, and no one gets it. Upon reaching 0 hearts, they should be banned from the server with the reason being "You have been eliminated". If a player has been eliminated the only way for the player to come back, would be another player crafting and using a "revive beacon". It's simply a beacon with a Gui with all eliminated players that can be crafted and used to revive someone.

Here's what I need the plugin to do (besides the life steal aspects above of course):

/withdraw - Allow players to withdraw a heart of theirs and get it as a physical item. (Do NOT allow players to withdraw so many hearts that it would eliminate them aka over withdraw hearts.)
- If said item is right-clicked it should redeem the heart item and give them a heart

OP Commands:
/giveitem Give the person a heart item or revive beacon
/reviveall Revive every eliminated player
/revive (player) Revive player by name
/lshealth get, set, add, subtract (player) 
- allows the getting of health value or setting it for a player
/lsrecipe See and setup the custom crafting recipe for the heart item and revive beacon

Additional Details: 

Obviously beside from the commands, the hearts and beacons need to have a way to be craftes and perferably a menu/gui to set this custom recipe. Again don't allow player to withdraw more hearts than what would leave them with one. So make sure they can't have less than 1 heart when withdrawing so it doesn't eliminate and ban them.

Im willing to negotiate a higher price if this is indeed a lot of work, im unsure of how much work it would take to make this, but I can pay more if this is a lot.

title: SEO consultant required to help succcessful SEO business build better reporting capabilities
description:
I run a successful SEO practice in a niche industry. I have many happy clients but parts of my SEO process, specifically around monitoring results and interpreting data, are extremely tedious/time consuming and/or don’t work well.

I’ve explained my issues below so that you can understand where I need help and determine if you’re the right person for the job.

1. Google Analytics - I have reasonable custom reports set up for all clients that should hypothetically give me an at-a-glance view of performance. However, there are two problems.
 a) We use SERPClix and an in-house version of SERP clicking to achieve higher search results. However, this traffic “pollutes” our data and therefore, our reports include traffic that is not real.
 b) The reports need to be converted to GA4.

2. Ahrefs - I use Ahrefs to track high value keywords. Once again, there are two problems.
 a) I don’t have a great way to measure performance over time. Ahrefs’ interface kind of sucks for that and I don’t really know what I should do to extract the data and view it in a better format.
 b) Using Ahrefs as a keyword tracking tool doesn’t allow me to surface any new keywords.

3. Google Search Console (GSC) - I have created a custom tool that uses a combination of exporting data from GSC manually and then running it through a set of scripts to help understand performance and surface new keywords to target. However, the solution is clunky and therefore I hate running the process.
 a) I’d like to explore using the GSC API to export data in a way that lets me a) track rankings/compare rankings with Ahrefs and b) surface new keywords to target. Also, note that the GSC data is also polluted by the SERP clicking so I am not sure what to do about that.

In an ideal world, I would find a solution that lets me integrate GA, Ahrefs and GSC data to track keyword performance over time and surface new keywords to target.

This solution may be an off-the-shelf solution that you will help me set up or it might be something custom that we’ll build together or with the help of a developer (I have many that could assist with basic API integration work).

title: Woocomerce to Shopify (Stripe payment processor) Migration
description:
Job Summary:

We are looking for an experienced E-commerce Website Migration Specialist to assist us with migrating our clients subscription-based e-commerce store from WooCommerce to Shopify. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of both WooCommerce and Shopify, as well as experience with subscription-based e-commerce stores and Stripe payment processing.

To Clarify: 

We already have the new Shopify site with products set up and it's actually live and using Yotpo subscriptions. 

What we need help with is migrating active/paying stripe customers from the woo-commerce to shopify so that we can shut down woo commerce and just use shopify with stripe and yotpo subscriptions side by side. 

Responsibilities:

- Collaborate with our internal team to understand the requirements and expectations for the migration
Conduct a thorough review of the current website to understand the customer subscription data and existing payment processes

- Develop and implement a migration plan that ensures a seamless transition from WooCommerce to Shopify without impacting existing customers

- Migrate all customer data, including billing information, shipping information, and subscription details, from WooCommerce to Shopify

- Test the migration to ensure that all customer data and subscription information has been accurately transferred
Ensure that all payment processing through Stripe is properly set up and integrated with Shopify to maintain the continuity of the subscription billing

- Provide ongoing support for any issues that arise during and after the migration, and develop strategies to mitigate risks of subscription churn

Requirements:

- At least 2 years of experience in website migration, with a focus on e-commerce sites and subscription-based models

- Strong knowledge of WooCommerce and Shopify, as well as the ability to work with various integrations, such as Stripe payment processing

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders

- Ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks and prioritise workload efficiently

- Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot and provide effective solutions to technical issues that arise

If you have any questions please let us know, looking for someone to implement asap. 

Looking forward to reviewing your proposal, Thank you!

title: Project on data mining
description:
Develop models to predict the response (y). For this, we need to be careful not to include variables
which may ‘leak’ information on the outcome being predicted.
Here, we want to examine how client characteristics can help predict response – so, only include the
client variables for developing modes to predict response.
Split the data into training and test sets – what proportion do you use for training?
For performance assessment of models:
- show confusion matrix and related performance measures - which measure do you look at, and
why? What do you conclude? What classification threshold do you use and why?
- show ROC based performance – ROC curve, AUC. What is the optimal threshold you obtain from
the ROC analyses, to get best accuracy?
- develop lift tables and assess performance.
(a) Develop rpart decision tree models.
(i) Parameters:
Do you find the prior parameter useful?
Determine the optimal cp value to obtain a best pruned tree. Describe how you go about doing this.
(ii) Variable importance: Which variables are important in the decisions by the tree model – discuss the
variable importance.
(iii) What is the performance of the model on training and test data?

(b) Develop C50 decision tree and rules.
(i) Parameters: Do you find the costs parameter useful? Describe how you use this.
 How many nodes are there in the tree? How many rules? Is tis what you expected?/
ii) Variable importance: Which variables are important in the decisions by the tree model and the
rules model – discuss the variable importance.
(iii) What is the performance of the tree model and rules model on training and test data?
(c) Develop random forest model.
(i) Parameters: Experiment with the m and number of trees parameters, Do you find performance to
vary? What parameters do you use to get your best model ? Explain how do you determine which
model is best.
ii) Variable importance: Which variables are important in the decisions - discuss the variable
importance.
(iii) What is the performance of the random forest model on training and test data?
(d) Develop gbm model
(i) Parameters: Experiment with the shrinkage and number of trees parameters, Do you find
performance to vary? What parameters do you use to get your best model ? Explain how do you
determine which model is best – you should use cross-validation.
ii) Variable importance: Which variables are important in the decisions - discuss the variable
importance.
(iii) What is the performance of the gbm model on training and test data?
(e) Develop naïve Bayes model.
(i) Parameters: look at the continuous variables in the data – do you think kernel density estimation
should be used? Does use of kernel density estimation help improve performance?
(iii) What is the performance of the naïve-Bayes model on training and test data?
(f) Compare performance of the different models you have developed.
(i) Show a table with comparative performance. Explain which performance measure you use for
this and why.
(ii) Plot the ROC curves in a single plot and compare. What do you conclude?
(iii) Cumulative lifts can be useful in assessing how a model will perform when implemented to
target customers. Discuss how lifts are useful in this context.
Compare models on their lift-based performance. Which model would you choose to implement
and why.
(iv) compare variable importance in the rpart, c50, random forest and gbm models. Discuss
similarities, differences

The first filter is VIX above or below a specific number at time of open.

close the condor when 95% of profits are realized or by 3:30pm on expiration day (Friday of the same week).

We are looking for a Squarespace Developer to work with our agency that develops websites for professionals in the therapy niche. title: Wordpress Site PageSpeed Optimization
description:
I've been running my sustainable travel blog, Arimo Travels (arimotravels.com), for five years now. I've done several tweaks here and there to optimize the site. I've mostly used WordPress plug-ins (Jetpack Boost, LiteSpeed Cache) and online guides for the fixing.

My skills are limited, and I haven't been able to solve all the issues on the site. Sometimes my tinkering has caused new problems, too. For example, I have a deactivated W3 Total Cache plug-in that I cannot delete as removing it breaks the site.

I would like you to go through my site's PageSpeed Insights ([link removed] and solve some of the biggest issues.

Some of the main issues are related unused Javascript and CSS, third-party code, and CLS. Google Ads play a big part in many of them. Other issues include font visibility and excessive DOM size.

There are a few restrictions to the updating. 

One: my site runs on my friend's server for free, so there's little that can be done with the server response time. Because of this, I'm also not sure if updating the PHP is possible.

Two: I use a plug-in called "Custom jQuery & CSS for Posts, Pages" on practically all my posts and pages. I use it for random generators (e.g. [link removed] and commentary tracks at the end of each post (e.g. [link removed] Some CSS/JS solutions have broken these interactive elements and button styles on my site, so I haven't been able to implement them.

As the posts and pages may have different issues as the front page, it might make sense to run the analytics on one of those as well: [link removed]

So, my main topics (in order of importance) are the following:
1) Improve page speed and solve issues on PageSpeed Insights
2) Improve custom CSS/JS implementation
3) Go through the plug-ins and streamline the library if possible.

The first topic is the most important, but if you think you can do more within the budget, you can also create solutions for the other two.

Contact me with a basic description of your solutions and what you could do with the budget, and we'll see if we could do something together!

If this role suits you, please share why!

A bit about us... Helm exists to free people and their potential.

In our work together, you'll doubtless discover both limitations and all that you need to catapult yourself beyond those limitations.

As a teenager, I discovered a near-paralyzing fear I had of public speaking when I was asked to give a talk. Years later, a communication coach shifted my paradigm. Soon after, I escaped my incapacitating dread and grew to love speaking.

What are your limitations? Some you may know. Some may be invisible. It's said that the worst prison is the one you don't know you're in. Elephants are born in parts of the world tethered to a stake in the ground and don't travel outside a 10-foot radius. By 1 year old, the elephant can snap the stake like a toothpick but it doesn't because it's been conditioned.

A big part of Helm is discovering our "growing edge" - the next realm of growth. And a big part of what animates our team at Helm is elevating each other beyond our conditioning and revealing the potential each of us has. But that is the only part.

Inspired by my own transformation, I spent over 20 years coaching individuals and organizations to break free from their limitations. While liberating, I learned that focusing just on success in my life or just "within the four walls of my business" isn't enough. And for one simple reason: freedom outside "our four walls" is vanishing and robbing us of our personal freedoms.

Threats to our freedom take many forms but they share 1 key feature: aggression. The core of my philosophy is the non-aggression principle: live and let live. Each of us should be in charge of our body, our property, and our money. If you have in you the fight to preserve freedom and individual liberty, it's my privilege to support and empower you however I can on your journey.

title: Small Business Marketing
description:
Hello, and thanks for taking a look at our posting on Upwork! Here’s a bit of information about us and what we need from a professional such as yourself…

Companah is a pet services business based in the middle of North Carolina. Yep, we deal with some sad pet owners - the core service of our business is pet cremation. You can learn more about us at [link removed] if you have time.

Here’s what we believe we need at this time. Let us know if you are interested in any or all of the deliverables (or if you aren’t completely sure of what we are asking for).

Deliverable 1 - Google Ad and Analytics Check Up

We’ve been running Google Ads for a while now (3-4 years), and we’d like to audit how we are doing and fine tune what we paying for (ads, targeted geos, rank). We are willing and able to do some of the work that you think we need to do on our web site (we’re considering a web site refresh anyway), but we don’t know what’s going on in the inner workings of search engines and the ads that they serve up.

Deliverable 2 - A Sliver of a Marketing Campaign

Companah has developed a new product for this service sector, and one that is kinda cool. We believe that this product can help us turn our service from a needed utility to a really great experience - and we want to advertise what that is. Storytelling and pets go together very well, and what we’ve developed maps along with that very nicely.

We think that the way to go about this is to have someone create some digital media (animation, video) that is targeted to our two market segments (pet owners, veterinary professionals) - but we are open to ideas as to the content of those videos as well as how they are delivered. Can you help us plan this?

Deliverable 3 - Media Content

Related to the second deliverable, we are looking for someone who can either create or help direct the creation of the materials related to marketing our new product.

Deliverable 4 - Digital Content

We’re an acute need business - pretty much the only time a pet cremation business shows up as a search result is because someone needs our service at that time. We believe we can change that.

Beyond the media content we noted in the third deliverable, we’d like some help in creating content that extends our organic presence. Pet stories, owner stories, caring for an aging pet, pet adoption stores, etc - we believe that there is a great amount of engaging content that we can share with our audience.

Access to Website Audit Report Generator Reputation Audit Report Generator

Local businesses

We are looking for a web developer to program our CMS (Content Management System). The CMS will be the place where the recipes for our mobile app will be created, so it will manage the content of the app. The CMS should be connected to our Rest API, which is still under development (but will be provided by us). 

There are multiple users with different roles in the CMS, depending on their role, certain pages and contents are hidden and cannot be accessed. In the Figma sketch, the left sidebar would adapt to the role of the logged-in user, so for example, "Home", "Recipes", "CMS Member", "App User", "Screen Layouts", "Media library", "Analytics" would be removed. Authentication is handled by AWS Cognito, and there is no registration, as it is an invite-only system. The initial users will be created by us, and from there on, additional users will be invited. They will receive a one-time password from Cognito, which they can use to log in. For login/authentication, we recommend NextAuth ([link removed]

When inviting a user, the name, surname, email, and role are set as shown in the Sketch. After logging in, the second most important thing is the creation of recipes and ingredients, as shown in the Figma Sketch. For each recipe/ingredient, a language is selected beforehand from a dropdown menu, as the recipes should be available in several languages. Two identical recipes or ingredients that only differ in language are still considered separate entries. The CMS can be programmed either in NextJs or SvelteKit (but Typescript is a must!). 
There are some more things I will explain in detail like for example the Screen Layouts section.
If you have any questions, feel free to ask. The UI design it self is not that important it should just work. You can use any component library you want or Tailwind CSS. I would appreciate some links(e.g. Github) to your previous work.

The stories you link to must also include a detailed workflow or steps for people to replicate the use cases if they want to.

1. I am looking for human stories. So stories by real people who used consumer-grade AI tools to do something interesting or useful. As opposed to a faceless company anecdote.

2. I am more interested in workflows with multiple steps rather than single-use cases or examples of individual prompts. Individual prompts are OK if it's a fascinating use case, but by and large, I'm looking for examples of how people incorporated AI into their workflow to make a meaningful change in their work or life. The stories must include exact steps and prompts so that I can recreate the workflow from the post. 

Here is a blog with stories I have found so far. This should give you a sense of what I'm looking for. Please don't cover any of the stories I have already written about [link removed]

To help make this clearer, I devised a simple rating system for the kinds of stories I'm looking for. The goal is to get as close to 10 points on each story as possible.

Who is the story about? (the more personal the story is the easier it is to relate to)
0 - Not sure
1 - An organization or agency, or group
2 - A person with a first and last name (the more famous the better, since it adds credibility to the story)

What was the problem they were solving with AI?
0 - AI is not solving a clear problem
1 - improving efficiency in some way
2 - solving a problem in a way non-AI alternatives just can't yet

How did they solve the problem?
0 - We don't know
1 - We have a general direction/idea of how they solved the problem
2 - We know the exact prompts/step they used

Do we know if it worked?
0 - we don't know if there was an improvement
1 - We can infer there was some improvement
2 - We have specific claims or stats around the improvement

Any considerations worth mentioning?
0 - No notes
1 point for adding best practices or gotchas worth paying attention to
1 point for plugging teh story into to a larger conversation/controversy around the issue/tool

To avoid any thoughtless, automated applications, please start your application with the sentence: I am not a robot.

title: Elite Direct-Response Marketing "Assistant" Needed To Work With CEO (1x in a lifetime opportunity?)

“I walked into Fran’s company as a marketing assistant.... And walked out a fv*cking direct-response legend.”

- You, in several years.

If you’re great at executing on, organizing and managing online marketing projects and people, then this might be the most important Upwork Job Listing you ever read.

In the next 3 minutes I’m going to utterly destroy any objection you have to considering an “assistant” role.

I will soothe and ease that voice inside you whispering “I’m overqualified for that title”, and quickly halt this voice’s effort to sabotage your career...

I will prove to you, beyond a shadow of doubt, that if you’re a talented up and coming marketer, this is far and away the best opportunity on planet earth right now.

Hi, I’m Fran Rengel.

And my superpower is creating high-converting video sales letters (VSLs). My VSLs have generated over $50 million for my businesses over the last 10 years, and almost $100 million more for other businesses.

Colleagues like Dan Ferrari, Justin Goff, Jon Benson, Chris Haddad and Ian Stanley consider me one of the best in the world at what I do. (If you want to see their video testimonials, check out [link removed]

My 5 year plan is to create the #1 direct response company in the world. And to do that, I need the right “right-hand man” (or woman) to assist me with (mostly marketing) tasks I no longer have the bandwidth for.

Sure, I could come up with some fancy job title to make this role sound more sexy… 

But at the end of the day, I’d rather hire someone humble enough to start as an “assistant”, and smart enough to see this job as the golden ticket it is.

And the truth is, you *will* be ASSISTING ME with things I no longer have the bandwidth for.

So yes, you will start as my “assistant”...

But by doing so, you will get invaluable business experience, as you see first-hand how we grow and scale our VSLs, witnessing mind-bending data about WHAT SELLS that virtually no one else has access to.

Your Responsibilities will include:

- Customer Avatar Creation
- Managing Split Tests
- Researching Supplement Ingredients
- Managing Upwork Contractors
- Writing Job Posts, And Giving Instructions
- Organizing Marketing Assets on Google Drive and Dropbox
- Creating Marketing Process Documents
- Sourcing VSL Spokespeople and Actors
- Delivering Page Design Instructions To Tech Team
- Conducting QA On VSL Videos

Within 3 months, you will complete these key outcomes:

- Complete Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all marketing processes related to our VSL product launch
- New research file completed for men’s health products (prostate and erection health). You will build a comprehensive file of customer research based on forums, competitor’s marketing materials, and surveys.
- 3 Upwork Hires Completed: You will use my upwork hiring process to create 3 job listings on upwork over the next 3 months. You will be in charge of choosing finalists, giving recommendations, and conducting a test project.

At this point, I hope to have scared off anyone who can’t handle this type of responsibility.

Much of your work will include CEO-level tasks that I’m currently doing, and will train you on directly.

I also hope to have scared off anyone with an ego too big to accept an “assistant role”.

If you prove yourself, your growth opportunities are endless here.

I want to end with an anecdote. In 2012, I was making close to 500k per year as CMO for a direct-response company.

Despite my success, I decided to work for Craig Clemens for FREE, on the side. Craig is the legendary copywriter who would later go on to found Golden Hippo.

That’s because I wanted to soak in every bit of knowledge I could from him. It was the best decision I ever made. I learned a lifetime of marketing knowledge from him.

Now, 11 years later, I believe that decision has come full circle. Only this time, it’s you who has the opportunity to make a decision and soak up a wealth of marketing knowledge.

Better yet, I’m not asking you to work for me for free…

You'll get PAID to have decades of knowledge uploaded into your brain. Knowledge that will put any $50K/year mastermind to shame.

(That being said, it will definitely won’t hurt your chances to give a discount in your proposal, if you believe this opportunity warrants it)

If you are not practically falling off the edge of your seat right now thinking “OMG I WAS MADE FOR THIS JOB AND THIS MOMENT”, then get the hell off this job listing right now. You’re not ready for this.

But if you’re thinking “fvck yes, this is the opportunity I’ve been waiting for”, then let’s do this… Send me a message with 1) your favorite movie, so I know you read the entire post 2) the best hourly rate you can offer me (likely 3-4 hours/day to start, may scale up to full time quickly) and 3) sell me on why I should pick you. Can’t wait to chat,
Fran

Buffer: Buffer is another social media management tool that allows you to schedule and publish posts across multiple social media platforms. The free version of Buffer allows you to manage up to three social media profiles and schedule up to 10 posts in advance.

title: Create data models from existing and apply ML to aid in prediction
description:
Our company ingests json data, applies a set of rules to it and outputs the resultant data classified into an existing industry standard classification system.

These rules are applied by an engine that essentially says, “if (value in json === ‘foo’) then (output1=’foo apple’, output2=’foo orange’). The rules engine algorithm pulls from a database table of known matches, and we update the table on an as-needed basis with new rules.

We have a considerable amount of ‘before (json)’ data and resultant outputs.

At the highest level, we are looking for help in developing an ML solution that will learn from these mappings and from future json data, getting better as it goes. 

A future, ML-informed iteration might then see ‘fooo’ in the json data and reasonably output then (output1=’foo apple’, output2=’foo orange’), as it predicted fooo is most likely foo.

Of course, much more detailed data and information are available for the project upon its start.

We envision this engagement as first, to determine how to structure the data properly to achieve the above; next, implementing an ML solution using that defined data and giving us the results we seek.

title: Help Tweak .NET 6 Console Application for JSON
description:
I have a license to use a commercial library called EdiFabric to process EDI files. It's provided as C# libraries and I use it for a very narrow purpose: serializing an input EDI file to JSON.

I do not really know/use C#, and my environment is Linux (Ubuntu LTS), so I basically compile a very lightly modified version of their sample app ([link removed] to a .NET 6 Console app, where it accepts a file path (args[0]), converts the file and outputs JSON to stdout (Console.Out.WriteLine(json.ToString());).

This works OK but I would like to solve the following issues:
1. I don't know how to allow for multiple input formats. Right now I actually have 4 mini-apps and they only differ from the ".OfType" call because I don't know how to set this dynamically. A command-line switch would be great, some light sniffing of the text to determine which converter to use would be even better.
2. I would like the input to come from stdin rather than having to write/read a tempfile. Their docs ([link removed] say "the reader takes System.IO.Stream as an argument so any stream of EDI data can be parsed" so this seems feasible.
 
BONUS -- the above 2 are what I really need, these additional ones would be nice eventually (and could be another quote if we get #1&2):
3. I currently output errors to stderr (Console.Error.WriteLine(issues.ToString());) and fold it into the JSON downstream. Would like if the errors can be in the same JSON output.
4. Converting the whole thing to an AWS Lambda would be very nice. (Note I have Lambda experience but not with the .NET runtime.)
5. Eventually deserializing the JSON back to an EDI file would be great -- this only applies to one of the file types, not all.

I have one restriction: due to the fact that this is a commercial license with a restricted serial number, and the sample files containing confidential information, all development will need to occur via screen share on my AWS instance. I will connect you to the Visual Studio box and then get out of your way. You don't need to teach me to code, just fix it -- but I can answer questions/test as we go if helpful.

I hope this all makes sense, I am very open to clarifying questions.

title: Custom Telegram Bot Needed
description:
We are running a viral marketing campaign within our React Native mobile app and one of teh key functions for users to perform is to join our Telegram Channel.

Our current flow is the following:
1. User is to use the @UserInfoBot to obtain their UserID
2. User copies their UserID and pastes it into the app field. App sends the UserID via an API to see if that user currently exists in the Channel
3. If the User has already been verified earlier and hence exists in our DB, User is prompted with that. If user doesn’t exist in our database records(because never verified before), we allow the user to click the button link to our channel.
4. User joins and goes back to the app and clicks verify button

It's a few more steps than I want. Here is the flow I would like.

1. User joins the Telegram channel. Our backend records this new entrant into our backend as unverified.
2. User enters their Telegram @username into the mobile app and the app will send the username to the backend to verify. If the entry is found, the flag is changed to verify. If the username could not be found, an entry will be entered in but until they actually join, this flag will remain unverified.

Your task as a rockstar Telegram Bot developer is to somehow use our existing Bot ID to send the @username and UserID of every new entrant to our backend via our API. We figured out that Rose bot can obtain the userID and @username of any entrant but it posts it in the channel. Rose bot can also delete any message so I was thinking of an automated process to print out the user info, record it in the backend, and then delete it as to not clog up the channel.

title: Wordpress/PHP developer for Woocommerce Subscription plugin
description:
What are we using?
For our Woocommerce shop, we are in need of custom development from a freelance developer. We are using the Woocommerce-Subscriptions plugin, through which our customers can make payments by installment.

This works like so: An order is made. This order get a unique ID. If the customer selects to pay by installments, Woocommerce creates a new “Subscription” with a unique ID. This subscription creates a new order with a new ID for each installment every month until all installments are paid. Thus, the “parent” subscription contains the initial order as well as all the automatically made orders from the installment.
The data from the Woocommerce orders in the Wordpress backend is passed to fields and contacts in our CRM. For this, we are using Zoho CRM / Zoho Books.

What kind of developer are we looking for?
- Can write custom code for Woocommerce (PHP)
- Has experience with the subscription plugin for Woocommerce 
- Would ideally speak German, otherwise English is fine

What do we need?
- We need some custom fields in our orders (not in the subscription!). These will then be passed to Zoho by us. We need:
Parent subscription ID. A field in each order, which has the unique ID of the parent subscription. Example: customer pays in 12 installments. Woocommerce creates an order (with unique ID) and, since it is a payment by installments, a subscription (with unique ID). The subscription now creates new orders each month, for the 11 remaining payments. The initial order as well as all the other automatically made orders should have the ID of the related subscription in a custom field.
- Number of current installment. Is this the first, third or 10th payment in the subscription? (Example: 4)
- Number of remaining installments. How many installments are still left in the subscription? (Example: 8)
- Total installments. How many installments are there in total in this subscription? (Example: 12)
- Total failed payments. How many times has the payment failed in this subscription? (Example: 2)

Tips/Help
A lot of the needed data and connections already exist in Woocommerce. Sadly, they are not available in the individual orders as fields, but in the parent subscription.
In the subscription overview, it is possible by default to see the number of paid installments, their IDs as well as the total failed payments.
By clicking on the subscription, one can easily see the initial order which triggered the subscription, as well as all the automatically made orders and their IDs. All of these orders should now have the parent subscriptions ID as a custom field, as well as the total installments, paid installments, the future/open installments and the total failed payments. (custom fields mentioned above)

Salary and further clarification 
For the development of these features, we have planned about 4 to 8 hours. We offer an hourly rate of €100/hour. We are happy to discuss details about the request for better understanding and clarification, as well as the salary. Sufficient budget is available in any case, should the job be more complicated than expected.

Here's my simple idea how to do it:
- Upload document, then extract text out of document, then feed into OpenAI API with the correct prompts. 

- There will be two issues; 
1. the API has a token limit so that will limit how much you can feed in and how much it can reply, and 
2. it won't remember the previous messages in the chat. 

Some are using Pinecone as "memory" by putting the embeddings in a database, which can work for semantic search, but not sure if that works to feed back into the OpenAI API.

title: Trade data analysis
description:
I am looking for assistance with a trade analysis project. 

The project is to acquire data from UN COMTRADE and then process it via comparison between different tariff regimes for trading partners for a group of countries.

The group and tariff rates to use would be identified to successful candidate. 

It is estimated at 8 days work.

STEP ONE
Using COMTRADE acquire data on global imports for a GROUP OF COUNTRIES as a group by value at 6 digit tariff code for sample year 2019.

STEP TWO 
Filter to top 100 imports by value (equating to minimum imports per line of approx. value of over 135,000 USD per annum for whole of GROUP OF COUNTRIES)

STEP THREE
Acquire the Applied MFN tariff being used in each of the countries within the GROUP for these top 100 tariffs and illustrate alongside the country specific tariff (to be provided) applied in 2023 and 2027.

STEP FOUR
Itemise for these 100 import lines the current MFN Applied rate, the Country specific duty rate for 2023 and the Country specific duty rate for 2027. 

STEP FIVE
Exclude all lines which are duty free under MFN Applied rate or which are excluded from country specific liberalisation. If less than 50 tariff lines remain, steps 1-5 above to be repeated until we have a minimum of 50 tariff lines to analyse. 

STEP SIX
Acquire country specific import data on those 100 import lines for each the 15 countries in the GROUP by volume and value; specifying top 3 MFN current exporters.

STEP SEVEN
Calculate unit cost per kg or litre for each tariff line

STEP EIGHT
Calculate Duty payable by unit under country specific agreement in 2023 and in 2027; and under Applied MFN per unit; and the total cost by volume/weight quoted for country specific agreement 2023, 2027 and MFN. 

STEP NINE
Calculate the Value of the switch in tariff for the GROUP buyer country from MFN to country specific tariff for 2023 and 2027 (total and by unit) 

STEP TEN
Produce abbreviated sheet illustrating the US dollar saving by unit and by total volume and giving a ranking of greatest saving by product line for each of 15 GROUP countries for 2023 and 2027.

title: Creative Director
description:
We are a fast-paced digital agency that provides innovative and creative solutions for our clients. Our team of experts is dedicated to delivering high-quality digital experiences that engage and inspire our clients' target audiences. We specialize in branding, web design and development, social media, and marketing.

We are seeking an experienced Creative Director to lead our creative team and oversee the development of all creative concepts and projects. The successful candidate will be responsible for creating and implementing innovative design strategies that align with our clients' goals and objectives. The Creative Director will work closely with the account management team to ensure all projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards.

Responsibilities:
• Lead and manage the creative team, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to ensure the team's success
• Develop and implement creative strategies that align with our clients' goals and objectives
• Collaborate with the account management team to ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards
• Conceptualize and oversee the development of all creative assets, including branding, web design, social media content, and digital marketing campaigns
• Ensure all creative output is on-brand, consistent, and aligns with the client's vision and objectives
• Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best practices to ensure our work is innovative and cutting-edge
• Work closely with external vendors and partners to ensure their work meets our quality standards
• Manage and oversee the creative team's workflow, ensuring all projects are delivered on time and on budget
• Develop and maintain relationships with clients to ensure their needs are met and expectations are exceeded
• Must be available during US PST time

Qualifications:
• 8+ years of experience in a creative role, with at least 3 years of experience leading a team
• Strong understanding of branding, web design and development, social media, and digital marketing
• Proven track record of developing and implementing successful creative strategies
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with internal and external teams
• Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
• Proficient in Adobe Creative Suite and other design software
• Experience working in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines.

If you are passionate about creativity and have the skills and experience to lead a team of talented designers, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity.

Please note, this is a full-time position working in a digital agency. If you are associated with a team or an agency please to not apply.

title: Portfolio Optimisation using Genetic Algorithms in R
description:
Portfolio Optimisation using GAs

You will investigate the development of a GA-based solution to optimise the weightings of a portfolio of assets and is composed of two parts:

Part 1

The focus of the first part of the assignment is on the optimisation of the portfolio using a GA. To begin with, manually choose a set of assets to work with - which ones you select are entirely up to you, but aim to work with around 10 and also try to pick ones which don't all exhibit the same behaviour (e.g. maybe take them from different sectors).

Then use a genetic algorithm (and the GA package) to identify the optimal set of weights for your portfolio which gives the best balance of risk versus return.

Having done this you then need to conduct a detailed evaluation of the portfolio by looking at how well it might perform in the "future", and comparing it with other possible portfolios (particularly a balanced portfolio, where all weights are even, and a set of randomly generated portfolios).

Finally (for this part) try exploring different weightings of risk and return. The idea behind this it to try and emulate a multi-objective approach and you will need to think about how it is possible to modify the fitness function to create differently balanced portfolios - e.g. at the extremes might be ones which only care about maximising returns or are very risk averse, and in between might be ones which prioritise risk over return and vice-versa. How do the weights and the performance of these portfolios compare with each other and your other solutions?

Part 2

Once you have done this successfully, then try extending your solution to select the set of assets for your GA to work on. The pool from which you select should be reasonably large (minimum of 50) and to begin with you may identify the selection criteria so that this GA operates independently of the one in part 1 (but would pass on the set of identified assets to be weighted by the GA from part 1). Once you have this working then investigate how these might work together (working out an efficient evaluation mechanism is the key to this part).

Further details are given below:

Criteria:

- Construction of a portfolio using the GA package (3)
- Evaluation of the portfolio on unseen "future" data (4)
To do this you will need to keep back some of your data (like a standard train/test split). For example, you might have trained your portfolio using data from 2019 to give you a set of weights. Then, keeping these weights constant, use them to calculate the returns from 2020 data. This should be a very simple calculation. Include your observations on this performance.
- Comparison of the evolved portfolio with balanced and random portfolios (5)
Is the portfolio you evolved any good? Compare and comment on the performance against an evenly balanced portfolio and the average of several runs of randomly generated portfolios. You could use run this comparison on both the training and the test data.
- Creation and evaluation of portfolios with differently balanced risk and return (to emulate a multi-objective approach) (6)
Within your fitness function your risk and return values will be evenly balanced. Modify this to create a number of differently balanced portfolios which give different preferences to risk or return. Report on the performance of these portfolios by considering how the weights and the performance of these portfolios compare to balanced (and other) solutions.
- Using GAs to select the assets (7)
Use a GA to pick the assets from a much larger set using a defined criteria. Report on the performance of this set (and make reference to the performance of portfolios using the approaches in part 1.
Integrate the two approaches so that the GA which is selecting the assets uses feedback from the GA that is optimising the portfolio. Again report on the performance of this approach, and compare it with others you have run.

title: Akeneo + BigCommerce connector experience
description:
We are looking for an expert in Akeneo + BigCommerce integrations. We've purchased the WEBKUL connector and need it properly integrated. 

Goal:
A working custom connector to send product data from Akeneo to BigCommerce and maintain the current shopping experience + full functionality of BigCommerce.
A custom connector is required to maintain/replicate the Product Display Pages in their current state (ex: Passing through Custom Swatches for options) – Webkul and other “off the shelf” connectors are missing features and functionality. The four missing requirements identified as necessary to use Akeneo are:
Must be able to map all native fields in BigCommerce
Must have method for adjusting the display type for variant options and modifier options (Custom Swatch, Radio Button, Rectangle List, Drop Down) - set for each option group
Must support Custom Swatches (manage in Akeneo) and pass through to BigCommerce
Must support mapping of Modifier Options to parent products (including support for display types as with Variant Options)

BigCommerce Native Fields
All native fields in BigCommerce should be mappable. List of native BigCommerce fields:
Item Type
Product ID
Product Name
Product Type
Product Code/SKU
Product UPC/EAN
Global Trade Item Number (GTIN)
Manufacturer Part Number (MPN)
Bin Picking Number
Brand Name
Option Set
Option Set Align
Product Description
Price
Cost Price
Retail Price
Sale Price
Bulk Pricing [bulk_pricing]
Fixed Shipping Cost
Free Shipping
Product Warranty
Product Weight
Product Width
Product Height
Product Depth
Allow Purchases
Maximum Order quantity [order_quantity_maximum]
Minimum Order quantity [order_quantity_minimum]
Product Visible
Product Availability
Track Inventory
Current Stock Level
Low Stock Level
Category
Product Image Files 1-20
Product Image IDs 1-20
Product Image Is Thumbnail 1-20
Product Image Sort 1-20
Search Keywords
Page Title
Meta Keywords
Meta Description
Product Condition
Show Product Condition
Sort Order
Product Tax Class
Stop Processing Rules
Product URL
Redirect Old URL?
Tax Provider Tax Code
Product Custom Fields
Is Featured Product
Variant Image
MODIFIER OPTIONS
Call for pricing label [price_hidden_label]
Show “Call for pricing” message instead of the price ? [is_price_hidden]
Attributes to be used as Product Video URLs
Product Image Descriptions 1-20

Note: BigCommerce attributes for Product Image Sort [Number] and Product Image Is Thumbnail should to be maintained but may not need to be separately mapped (ie. images should display in the same sort order and the same images used for thumbnails), though these may not need to be separate attributes if this can be accomplished in a different way, for example, by making sure that the images are mapped/imported in the correct order).

BigCommerce Variant Options
There are 4 display types for variant options. User should be able to designate the appropriate display type for each variant option (will vary depending on the product and variant option).

The Type for each attribute designates how it will be displayed on the Product Display Page (PDP) (ex: Those with Type=Swatch are displayed with an image thumbnail). Custom Swatches are also used with Modifier Options.

BigCommerce Custom Swatches
The connector needs to support designating a separate image for each attribute option used for variants (and modifier options).

Other connectors either allow only for one variant display type to be used for all variant options and only support the usage of hex codes – connector accommodate the usage of Custom Swatches (a thumbnail image used to represent the option visually. 

BigCommerce Modifier Options
Modifier options are used to configure or customize products but do not alter the SKU when selected. Modifier options are stored at the parent product level and are critical to allowing our customers to configure products.

Records for Modifier Options in BigCommerce include a Name, Type, list of Value options, a Default option designation, and Required Yes/No.

The Attribute Label in Akeneo will be used for the Name for the modifier option in BigCommerce. 

The Type for each attribute designates how it will be displayed on the Product Display Page (PDP) and should be handled similarly to Variant Options to preserve the way these product options are displayed (ex: Those with Type=Swatch are displayed with an image thumbnail).

Option values designated as "Default" indicate those that are preselected without customer interaction.

Loom video to help explain and for clarity:

We have a client in need of a trainer to deliver an API First Design skills course.

Training Location: Remote

Class Size - 12

Class duration: 2 days (14 Total Course Hours)

Training Dates: TBA ASAP

Training Fee: We are willing to pay between $800.00-$1,000.00 per day all-inclusive for training (Depending on Experience)

Timeframe: The Client looking to get this training scheduled/confirmed as soon as possible and will need to meet with the trainer and approve their Statement of Work.

**Please include resume with proposal to be considered for this opportunity**

Overview
API First Design refers to the practice of prioritizing the target developer's interests by firstly designing a very good API, then building software on top of that. This approach advocates laying down a strong foundation for others to build on.

This instructor-led, live training (online) is aimed at developers who wish to enhance the efficiency with which APIs are developed while improving the quality, reliability, and reusability of the APIs.

By the end of this training, participants will be able to:

Plan and organize a software project around API first design concepts.
Discuss agree on a shared vision of the API with other stakeholders.
Evaluate and adopt the tools needed to efficiently implement an API first approach.
Develop software in parallel with other team members.
Reduce the cost of developing software applications.
Format of the Course

Interactive lecture and discussion.
Lots of exercises and practice.
Hands-on implementation in a live-lab environment.
Course Customization Options

To request a customized training for this course, please contact us to arrange.
Course Outline
Introduction

Overview of API First Design

The Benefits of an API-First Approach

Brainstorming the Product and its Requirements

Identifying and Understanding the API Stakeholders

Setting up the Development Environment

Creating an API Contract

Creating an API Style Guide

Establishing Design Standards to Ensure API Governance

Automating Key Processes (Documentation, Validation, Mocking, Versioning, etc.)

Creating Additional APIs

Organizing and Managing an API Portfolio

Monitoring the APIs

Collaborating with Internal Developers

Troubleshooting

Summary and Conclusion

title: Graph Database Architect
description:
Data Architect / Developer - Job Description
 
This is a freelance opportunity to provide guidance to the team with the potential for a permanent role if desirable. 

About the Company 
Mission. Zeki puts the best global talent at the centre of today's science to accelerate innovation. Scientists use numerous ways to improve their skills, publish their work, broaden their network, seek funding and commercial opportunities. Zeki is building an information service which collects diverse data sets then uses behavioural analytics and AI to discover insights into the performance and potential of global science talent. We are creating a new benchmark for evaluating science talent.

About the Role
Exciting opportunity for a hands-on Data Architect with some data engineering, BI and software development skills to take ownership of the data models and data platform for a startup business. 

This will suit someone who is strong with data modelling (relational, dimensional, graph) and likes learning and building new solutions to complex data challenges using cloud technologies. This will include big data processing, data integration, data enrichment, database performance management, data caching techniques, data quality initiatives, entity resolution, web scraping, orchestration and building CI/CD pipelines, participating in machine learning operations and BI solutions using PowerBI.

You will have good experience of the data development process, including requirements gathering, database design, modelling and development, writing complex SQL queries, query performance tuning and developing a semantic layer with BI tools. 
 
Good communication skills and a self-learner, able to quickly acquire new skills and take ownership of a complex, multi-layered data platform. You will be working closely with the research analysts, data engineers and data scientists to build and maintain a complex data platform environment which is fundamental to the business success. 
 
Any experience of entity resolution, graph database or behavioural analytics is highly desirable.

Responsibilities
• Lead the data modelling of diverse datasets and hands on development of the database 
• Build an understanding of the business model and be able to translate this into the models
• Be part of the operational support of the data platform to ensure a reliable service
• Track and communicate issues with the data platform to the technology leadership team
• Document the delivered solutions at the technical and business level

Skills
• Good experience with database modelling and deploying database schema changes
• Good experience with cloud platforms and serverless computing (AWS, Lambda)
• Solid experience in complex SQL query logic, analysis and performance tuning 
• Some experience of data analytics on cloud platforms: AWS, Azure or GCP
• Complex SQL queries to interrogate data and join datasets
• Scripting and programming languages (Python, Django, node.js, C#)
• Ability to manage large sets of messy data and organise it effectively 
• Experience with modern BI tools and semantic layer: Tableau, PowerBI
• Experience of close collaboration with data scientists and Machine Learning engineers
• Strong experience with REST APIs for extracting external data
• Experience with web scraping techniques highly desirable
• Creating and documenting technical design specifications
• Experience in working in virtual teams and being in constant collaboration 
• Ability to work unsupervised and take ownership for key services

Nice to Have
• An understanding of data lake, data warehouse and dimensional modelling techniques
• Experience with entity resolution and behavioural analytics
• Experience with graph database for exploring relationships across multiple datasets
• ETL architectures and tools, including integration with APIs, coding Python data pipelines
• Team leadership skills to manage tasks and run standups 

We offer a friendly, collaborative working environment with a high level of autonomy and time for exploring innovative technology ideas in a fast-paced start up model. 

Our Values. At Zeki, we believe that a great culture is key to our personal well-being and professional success. As a founding team, we live and work through these values and behaviours. We will ask the same of you if you come and work with us.
• Trust: We assume the best in others and we communicate with clarity and consideration. 

• Respect: We respect and include a diversity of talents and perspectives and welcome all points of view. 

• Integrity: We believe in the purpose of our work and seeing everything in the round.

• Novelty: We find frontiers to break through and challenge the orthodoxy.

- record in portrait mode

Ideas:
- If you have more than one ball at hand, use different ones. ideally 5-10 cm in diameter. Could possibly work with larger ones too but the ideal ball is smaller than a football and larger than a golf ball, closer to a tennis ball...
- use different rooms and different walls with varying textures on the floor and wall, with carpet, without carpet etc
- do it from different angles
- Potentially you could handhold the camera in 10-30% of them so that there is some movement, nothing och erratic though. For at least half of them: put the phone camera on a stand or prop it up against something to get a completely static image without any camera movement
- Use a smartphone camera, but if you can, use more than one phone so that the variation in optics etc are represented
- a varying amount of random background noise would be good too. Sometimes complete silence, sometimes a tv on, someone doing the dishes, whatever you can come up with that might happen in a household
- hands in the shot, no hands, feet, ...: all ok, again, variation is good
- the start and end does not have to be perfectly timed, it is a good thing if a minority of the clips include picking up the phone, laying down the phone or framing incorrectly at the start/end, like a normal user would if this was part of a mobile ar game

For each video file, count the number of bounces against the wall. then create a text file next to the video file with the same name but a different extension. Example:

IMG_3221.mov
IMG_3221.txt

Keep the video filename as it comes out of the phone, that’s fine, doesn’t have to be exactly IMG_…

In the text file, add your observations, using the structure below. After each colon, specify bounce count and ball color. And for type specify either steady or handheld.

bounces:
color:
type:

Or if you prefer, you can use a Google sheet or excel and use the corresponding columns i.e filename, bounces, color, type, with each video clip on its own row.

Perhaps this is a quicker workflow than the text files? The data is easy to consume either way

Why do all of this? We are training a machine learning model that once trained on a sufficient amount of data, is supposed to be able to watch other videos and make good predictions about ball color and no of bounces. We intend to do this visually but might also attempt to do it by audio analysis, so variation in the audio situation is good too - including making noises a naive mode might interpret as a ball bounce

If the AI model eventually gets good enough it might be used in a mobile game where the user is supposed to bounce a ball and the app keeps track of the count automatically.

title: Web app development to assist with escape room game
description:
I need a web app developed that will be used alongside physical escape room games that I have built. Its role will be to grant access to the game, keep a timer running of how long the game is going in, record when the game is complete, and provide hints along the way if the player needs help. Below is a description of some of my requirements.

Definitions:

Clues: Required pieces required to solve or aid in solving a puzzle to unlock a lock or gain access to a new part of the game. Could be a video clip, audio, text, 
Hints: information given to the player to aid them in solving a puzzle, these are not required but exist to help players out that may be having trouble with a puzzle.
Puzzle: A contrived problem that is created by the game creator. Could be a riddle, a concealed code, and encrypted message.
Game: A series of puzzles together with a loose plot that the player is trying to get completed in the shortest amount of time possible.
Prop: A physical piece of a puzzle

Apps purpose:

1. Allow access to game

Play scan’s QR code on the game this will take them to the Web app.

They will have to provide a game code (which they will have gotten when they purchased the game rental) Game codes are unique and will be used to track the game/customer. 

The website should have a database of valid game codes, and when the game is complete the code will not be able to be used again.

Once a player logs in they are prompted to create a team name, this will be used on the leaderboard if they get a high score. Log their IP address, browser, and any other information we can grab and link to their game code. 

Once the player is logged in it will take them to the main working part of the app and reveal to them the first clue of the game. 

2. Track game progress

Game events (Eg game start, hints, qr code clues throughout the game, and game complete) and times will be stored in a database linking them to the game code.

This will be used to keep track of the teams score as well as for analytics on how the game is going and what puzzles are working well or might need modification.

3. Show video, audio, or text clues

Throughout the game there may be a qr code that is revealed the player will scan that and be given a clue for their next puzzle.

4. Provide hints / help to game players

Next to each lock will be a QR code for the player to scan in case they need a hint or are stuck. Once they scan the QR code it will give them a clue for that puzzle. (As well as record the hint used) 

If they are still stuck they can scan it again for an additional hint, and possibly an additional hint, with the final one just giving them the code to the lock.

5. Instruct player on how to reset the game and capture photos showing it’s done properly

Walk the player through how to reset the game for the next player. Prompting to take pictures so that it can be confirmed by game rental location.

Additional thoughts to keep in mind:

I would like to be able to add games and changes hints fairly easily without a lot of programming.

I would like to be able to easily have the logo and branding changed for the game. The idea being that a game can be licensed and made for say Exit Escape Games and everything is completely branded for Exit Escape games. My company branding is completely hidden and behind the scenes.

I am thinking that a web app is the way to go so that I don’t have to worry about phone OS’s and app store bullshit. Heroku or whatever.

title: Corporate Real Estate Company needs Content Editing/Writing for Marketing Collateral (and more)
description:
Presidio Bay Ventures, Inc. (“PBV”) is a real estate investment and development firm headquartered in San Francisco. Our team is focused on sourcing and structuring unique, value-add investment opportunities that generate attractive risk-adjusted returns and our primary expertise is in new construction and major renovation of complex, large-scale office, multifamily and other special-use facilities. Since its formation in early 2012, PBV has executed on $4Bn+ of transactions through 37 projects across seven states, representing over 4.1M square feet of development.

Presidio Bay uses copy writers and content writers for the following main deliverables: 

-- Synthesis of forward-facing market positioning documents for each of our real estate projects
-- Research and ghostwrite Thought leadership white papers focused on real estate trends
-- Content editing for long-form monthly reports which are compiled by several team members. The content editor would be responsible for creating a consistent tone of voice and labeling of dates and entities throughout the report, and ensuring all information is written in complete sentences and complete thoughts. 
-- Editing and content / copy writing of forward-facing marketing deliverables like corporate marketing presentations and project websites. 

This particular project is a two-part project with a quick turn-around expectation (~2 weeks). It can also be considered a chance for us to get acquainted with your work. Ideally, we would like to connect with 1 or more strong writers to assist with the above tasks on regular and/or ad hoc basis. 

The Task: 

Part 1 - Acquaint yourself with our company by reviewing our Firm Overview Presentation and the current corporate website (more information on these documents is outlined in the 'Resources' section below). Using the information from these two assets, please complete a full review of our draft Advisory Services presentation and suggest copy edits, refinements and additions to effectively convey our company brand and product offerings. Once finalized, move to second part. 

Part 2 - Presidio Bay is launching a new corporate website in the next month. We'd like your help conducting a complete review of the staging link to ensure that our brand is coming through effectively for all future users. During your review of the website experience, please focus on the short and long-form copy, taking opportunities to drop in any copy from the Firm Overview and the Advisory Services deck, plus any new copy that you may write to ensure that the text flows and reads well throughout, and the website is engaging and comprehensive about the various aspects of our business. Please keep in mind that we want to effectively convey who Presidio Bay is and what we do. Specifically, we ask that you look at things like consistency in tone of voice and nomenclature; one example is the use of PBV vs Presidio Bay vs Presidio Bay Ventures, etc. Additionally, we want to be sure that any ‘Lorem Ipsum’ is replaced with suggested copy (there isn’t much of this, if any). Please don’t assume that we are absolutely set on any of the copy that is currently showing (aside from the individual Thought Leadership articles and their corresponding posts), we want you to feel free to make suggestions freely. One note I have on the Expertise and team bio sections – please review with a critical eye on length and consistency in tone of voice (use of we/us/our and addressing people using the first name (preferred) vs last name). If some bios or Expertise sections are much longer than others, please suggest a redacted version that still captures the salient points. 

Please note that despite this being a staging link for a website that’s still in development, you are not responsible to look for or review for any bugs in the UX interface. That said, if you do find anything that feels confusing or broken, we would be grateful for a quick flag. We are in the process of adding a few remaining visual assets in various locations so please feel free to overlook these areas. 

Resources: 

We will provide our Firm Overview presentation and live company website as resources to get acquainted with our brand story, values, style and tone of voice prior to making recommendations about the Advisory Services deck and new website. Please note that the Firm Overview is constantly being evolved and updated, and as such has a few slides that may be marked with “Update.”

The chatbot should also include a button in the bottom right corner of the responses field that allows users to listen to the responses out loud.

The dedicated webpage should be in keeping with the branding and look of the existing website, and should include text fields to the left and right of the chat window that the website owner can easily edit to add things like disclaimers or limitations.

title: Help needed with WordPress issues
description:
Hello,

I've been keeping my Wordpress website up for some years. I'm stuck now with some issues, of which three more urgent ones. I'll describe them first in one line, then more extensively. It would be great to find someone who can fix all issues, the first three in the very short term.

1. mySql database has been exploding recently, because of some unnecessary log saving.
2. WP keeps telling me I need to use a persistent object cache. My website provider is ovh.com.
3. A scan on semrush apparently indicates issues with 'mixed content', which could be bad for my seo/sem.
*Then a few less urgent things, but would be nice to have them solved*
4. "Page cache is detected but server response time is still slow" (sometimes)
5. "A scheduled event is late. The scheduled event, action_scheduler_run_queue, is late to run. Your site still works, but this may indicate that scheduling posts or automated updates may not work as intended."
6. I would like to have reCAPTCHA set up for my contact forms, but don't succeed.

Below I describe those issues more extensively. Here first some extra info:
- A few months ago I wanted to clean up my website to make it faster. I de-activated almost all plugins, only re-activated those I really need and got rid of the others. The website was then superfast (confirmed by Gtmetrix). But not for long, so some things are not like they should.
- The website has a simple webshop, which is directly connected to my POS/EMS software.

1. mySql database is exploding. This happened almost two years ago as well. The database has been keeping a stable size of less than 100Mb, but suddenly with every backup it significantly increases in size, to soon get over its maximum limit of 400Mb. The problem returned apparently after 'cleaning up' my website as described above. Probably I overwrote the fix that one guy had made then. The issue was just a few lines of the database exploding in size. This is what he wrote back then:
"So as I suspected there are issues of LOG files being saved into the database. This is caused by different plugins including woocommerce itself and WPFORM lite. So this means that there are many scheduled actions running on the background. I can check to reduce the retention period of every running hooks to 1 day or 1 week for example. Then the log data will be emptied automatically."

2. WP keeps telling me I need to use a persistent object cache. My website provider is ovh.com. Not sure what more I can describe here...

3. A scan on semrush.com apparently indicates issues with 'mixed content'. This scan was done by a guy who will help me with google ads. He noticed this might be a reason why my ads don't get displayed. However I can't find any other indications of that issue.

4. "Page cache is detected but server response time is still slow". I have the Super Cache plugin installed, but WP is not entirely happy yet

5. "A scheduled event is late. The scheduled event, action_scheduler_run_queue, is late to run. Your site still works, but this may indicate that scheduling posts or automated updates may not work as intended." I had some cron-plugin installed but didn't get it solved with that.

6. I would like to have reCAPTCHA set up for my contact forms, but don't succeed. Something just doesn't want to go.
